As we wrap up, let's bring together what we've discovered.
The world's promises don’t mean much unless someone has the courage to step up—especially when it really counts.
Bearing witness, even when it feels impossible to act, is something we owe each other.
Healing after such deep pain? It’s never quick or easy. It takes time, honesty, and a willingness to reckon with what’s happened.
Justice and accountability matter, but so does finding compassion for everyone involved—even when that’s the hardest thing to do.
And maybe the most important lesson? Stopping future tragedies is a responsibility we all share, no matter when or where we live.
The story of Rwanda, seen through the eyes of those who lived it, reveals not just the depths of cruelty, but also the heights of resilience.
It’s tempting to look away, to think these problems are just too big, or that someone else will step in. But every action—no matter how small—truly matters.
The survivors, and those who tried to help, show us that hope can hold on, even in the darkest moments.
So if you ever start to doubt whether your choices make a difference, remember Rwanda.
Remember that staying silent and doing nothing comes at a cost—but so does choosing courage and compassion.
Let this story be a reminder to notice what’s happening around you, to speak up, and to reach out—because the work of building a kinder, more humane world never really ends.
And it needs all of us.
